key_insight: Func-R1 shows that multimodal math reasoning over functions fails when models ignore visual cues, so it explicitly combines visual grounding with symbolic reasoning to reduce modality interference.
engineering_relevance: The work is relevant for building MLLMs that can reliably solve graph- and plot-based engineering math problems where reading the figure correctly is as important as the equations.
method: Explicitly decouples perception from reasoning in the model architecture.
Uses a hierarchical post-training pipeline to first identify critical visual evidence and then perform deeper theoretical reasoning.
Introduces PATO to align policy updates with mathematical theory while correcting heterogeneous visual information during reasoning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive benchmark evaluation across diverse tasks, with Func-R1 achieving the best open-source MLLM performance and a reported 8.4% gain over GPT-5 on MathVerse function-oriented tasks.
watch_item: The method may depend heavily on benchmark-specific visual cues, so robustness to noisier diagrams or out-of-distribution plots should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Func-R1: Incentivizing Mathematical Function Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
